provenance: PR #60 R16. Round 3's guard covers four string-valued inputs — `name`, `text`, `near` and `anchor` — and shipped cases for three of them. `anchor` is not a target key at all: it is a top-level plan key the executor passes to `resolve` separately, so a model can emit `"anchor": 4.82` and the plan lint, which validates target KEYS, never sees it. Base `6b016b5` and `fb84a88` raised `AttributeError: 'float' object has no attribute 'strip'` inside `_loose` and classified the step `act`; the guard changed that class to `locate` with nothing covering the change. Failure class is a graded output (INV-1), so a class that moves silently is exactly what this repo grades.

triage.red_first: the case did not exist. On `fb84a88` (the tree before the guard) the same plan is `failure:act` — `AttributeError: 'float' object has no attribute 'strip'`; on `4bda01f` it is `failure:locate` and nothing asserted either. The guard is right and it was ungraded, which is the finding.
triage.note: `invariant` with its three siblings — `resolver-non-string-name-is-a-locate-failure`, `resolver-non-string-near-is-a-locate-failure`, `resolver-non-string-name-is-a-list` — because they are must-always-hold diagnosis properties and the `fast` band cannot pay for them. `resolver-non-string-target-is-a-locate-failure` (the `text` key) stays in `fast` as the representative, which is why SKILL.md now says four keys and four siblings.
